chunks: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani told us, saying: Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id in the City told us, saying: Azhar ibn Kumail told us, saying: Al-Mu'tamar ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I read for Fudayl ibn Maysara, from Abu Jareer, that Abu Burda told him, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, saying:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, said: Three will not enter Paradise: one addicted to wine, one addicted to magic, and one who cuts kinship ties. And whoever dies addicted to wine, Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will make him drink from the River of Ghouta. It was said: And what is the River of Ghouta? He said: A river that flows from the genitals of harlots, and their smell harms the people of the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What are the three people who will not enter Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to elucidate the specific punishment for wine addiction, linking the sensory experience of Hell to the source of the sin. The River of Ghouta, flowing from the genitals of harlots, serves as a poetic justice where the wine-addict is afflicted by the foul odor of those whose bodies were the vessels of intoxication's allure. This imagery underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical and spiritual consequences of major sins, particularly the degradation of the self through addiction.
